You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: NumericEntityUnescaperTest.testSupplementaryUnescaping() passes the decimal numeric entity "𐰢" and expects it to unescape to the supplementary Unicode code point U+10C22, represented in UTF-16 as the surrogate pair "\uD803\uDC22".
- What happens: In org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaper.translate(CharSequence, int, Writer), after parsing the numeric value, the code does:
  - out.write(entityValue); (line 63)
- Why this is wrong: Writer.write(int) writes a single 16-bit char. For code points above 0xFFFF (supplementary characters), this truncates the code point to its lower 16 bits, losing the higher plane. Here, 68642 (0x10C22) gets truncated to 0x0C22, producing the single BMP character U+0C22 instead of the surrogate pair "\uD803\uDC22".
  - With StringWriter (used by CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence)), write(int) appends exactly one char, confirming this truncation.
- Evidence from surrounding translation flow:
  - CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence, Writer) is code point-aware and writes default characters with Character.toChars(Character.codePointAt(...)) when no translator consumes input (lines 83–104). The translator contract comment even notes they “have to understand codepoints” (line 92).
  - NumericEntityUnescaper.translate violates this by emitting a single char for any entity value, including supplementary code points.
- Consequence: The unescaping of "𐰢" produces a single BMP character (U+0C22) rather than the expected surrogate pair for U+10C22, causing the assertion failure in the test.
- Secondary note: NumericEntityUnescaper.translate returns a “consumed” count equal to the number of input characters that formed the entity (e.g., 8 for "𐰢"), whereas CharSequenceTranslator’s loop treats “consumed” as “number of code points consumed” (comment on line 86). While this mismatch does not break this particular test case (the loop still skips past the entity), it indicates a separate contract inconsistency. The primary failure here, however, is the incorrect writing of supplementary code points.

Root cause:
NumericEntityUnescaper.translate writes the parsed entity value with Writer.write(int), which only writes a single UTF-16 char and cannot represent supplementary code points. It should emit the surrogate pair using Character.toChars(entityValue) (e.g., out.write(Character.toChars(entityValue))).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
